open_findings.title: Reject invalid owner entry and exit before mutating ownership state
open_findings.evidence: A closed online-read Owner can enter again and open a second database; __exit__ then stops at _close_attempted before cleanup. Observed opens=2, closes=1, active=True, guard depth=1, held=False. Recursive proof-owner entry overwrites an owned connection. Wrong-thread exit invalidates rightful owner, raises AttributeError from thread-local owner stack, and leaves guard depth=1.
open_findings.required_change: Use single-use entry state before thread/guard mutation; reject reused/reentrant/wrong-thread entry and invalid/wrong-thread exit without disturbing the valid active owner. Keep cleanup state changes within the owning thread and preserve the original error.

open_findings.title: Enforce diagnostic and proof read statement capabilities, not first FROM table
open_findings.evidence: While process is held, diagnostic guard-proof owner returns business subject alice from SELECT u.subject FROM operation_authority a JOIN users u ON 1=1. _query_limit finds only operation_authority, so joined business SQL is admitted.
open_findings.required_change: Restrict proof/discovery/schema-reference observations to exact reviewed statements; refuse joins, unions, subqueries and alternate SQL outside that statement set before execution. Keep queued_ids exception outside diagnostics only.

open_findings.title: Constrain barrier and started-receipt writers to their actual roles
open_findings.evidence: Both store.write(role=barrier) and store.write(role=started-receipt) commit UPDATE users SET active=0 WHERE subject=alice with no new intent and held=False. Generic mutation regex admits all business tables for both roles.
open_findings.required_change: Use explicit role-specific statement allowlists for durability barrier and started-receipt writes. Refuse business mutations and additional SQL clauses before native execute; test admitted statement behavior and forbidden cross-role mutations.
